Eno

Eno is a historical people name associated with North Carolina’s Piedmont and the Eno River. The linked state plan and historical reference support this limited geographical introduction; later histories and descendant connections need further review.

GovernmentNorth Carolina Division of Parks and RecreationSource 1Supporting reference · outside substantive inspected count

Eno River State Park General Management Plan — North Carolina Division of Parks and Recreation ↗

The state plan identifies Eno people living along the Eno River at early European contact. Jean B. Anderson's Library of North Carolina account independently locates the historical Eno in North Carolina's Piedmont. This supports a historical North Carolina connection without assigning a modern Eno government or adopting uncertain descendant-identification claims. Inspection: Actual PDF cover, mission text and printed page 3 (PDF page 2), II. HISTORY, especially lines 31–34 identifying Eno, Shakori and Occoneechee along the river. Supporting Anderson, Eno Indians (2006), first geographic paragraph was read in complete indexed article text; direct NCpedia fetch returned 403. No old profile source was reused. Supporting geographic excerpt; excluded from the substantive profile-source target.
